Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached are three artifacts that address each of your bullets: a one-page narrative, a compartmentalization diagram, and our RFI response matrix. The high-level points up front:

- Tenant isolation: logical multi-tenancy with strict per-tenant namespaces; no shared persistent model state. For dedicated/private deployments we provide isolated runtime pools (single-tenant compute) and optional host-level enforcement using VPC service controls.
- Control plane vs data plane: control plane handles orchestration (model routing, telemetry) over a management network; inference traffic (data plane) runs in customer-dedicated subnets with optional sidecar egress proxies.
- KV cache handling: ephemeral KV cache lives on memory-backed volumes within the serving pod; caches are not checkpointed to shared storage by default and can be pinned to a customer-managed encrypted store if required.
- Egress controls & exfil prevention: allowlist-only outbound via egress proxies, TLS inspection at gateway when enabled, per-tenant flow logs, and content-aware filtering for token patterns. We also support network-level bastions, NAT gateway restrictions, and HSM/KMS-bound encryption for sensitive keys.

Attached: compartmentalization-diagram.svg; rfi_response_matrix.xlsx; kv-cache-architecture.png

Alex — quick follow-up from the infra side. Below are the concise threat-memory points and a mitigation rubric; I'm keeping this focused so you can paste into the RFP.

1) East-west token leakage (threat): an attacker with access to a serving host could read KV cache or intercept in-flight requests.
   - Mitigation: KV cache lives in ephemeral memory; processes run as non-root; we recommend kernel lockdown + seccomp for private deployments. For hosted customers, diskless caches and strict container isolation reduce risk.

2) Lateral movement between customer workloads (threat): misconfigured network ACLs or shared orchestration plane could allow pivoting.
   - Mitigation: Strong namespace separation, per-tenant VPCs for Private mode, control-plane authenticated RPCs over mTLS, and eBPF network policies to enforce pod-to-pod allowlists.

3) Unauthorized egress/exfiltration (threat): data leaving via third-party integrations or misrouted responses.
   - Mitigation: Outbound allowlist enforced by an egress proxy, token redaction at gateway for PII patterns, and configurable response hooks to drop or redact fields. We include per-request audit trace IDs for reconstruction.

Canary test idea (for your infra): deploy a single-tenant runtime in your VPC with egress-proxy allowlist configured to a staging endpoint; run a synthetic workload that attempts simulated key exfiltration and verify logs + automatic blocking. Naomi/Stephanie — we can provide a terraform module and runbook.

— Markus
